title: US Sanctions Raipur CEO and Firm for Supplying Explosives to Sudan's Armed Forces
excerpt: Alok Choudhari and SBL Energy Limited are among eight individuals and entities blacklisted by the US Treasury for fuelling Sudan's civil war.
body:
• The US Treasury has sanctioned Alok Choudhari, CEO of Raipur-based SBL Energy Limited, for allegedly supplying over 200 shipments of explosives to Sudan's armed forces
  • SBL Energy, also known as Amin Explosive Private Limited, was among eight individuals and entities sanctioned for fuelling Sudan's civil war
  • The sanctions target networks supporting both the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, which Washington has accused of genocide
  • The US also sanctioned international recruitment networks supplying former Colombian soldiers to fight alongside the RSF

An Indian CEO in the Crosshairs

The US Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control has imposed sanctions on Alok Choudhari, the CEO of Raipur-based SBL Energy Limited, accusing the Indian national and his company of supplying explosives that prolonged Sudan's devastating civil war.

According to OFAC, SBL Energy — also known as Amin Explosive Private Limited — shipped more than 200 consignments of explosives and explosive-related materials to Target Multiactivities Company (TMAC), a Sudan-based firm that maintains the Sudanese Armed Forces' arsenal. The explosives were subsequently used in bombs deployed by the SAF against both the rival Rapid Support Forces and civilian populations.

Eight Entities Blacklisted

Choudhari and SBL Energy were among eight individuals and entities sanctioned in the latest tranche of US measures aimed at choking off the supply chains fuelling Africa's worst humanitarian crisis. The Treasury Department also blacklisted TMAC and its general manager, Tariq Hussain Muhammad Madani, a senior officer linked to Sudan's Defence Industries System.

"These networks supply weapons, explosives, and foreign fighters to both the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. Their support has prolonged a conflict that has created the world's worst humanitarian crisis and provided space for terrorist groups to operate."

— Tommy Pigott, US Department of State spokesperson

The sanctions also targeted Ports Engineering Company Ltd., accused of importing military uniforms, ammunition belts, and weapons equipment for Sudanese security agencies. Separately, the Treasury expanded sanctions against an international recruitment network that supplies former Colombian soldiers to fight alongside the RSF.

Sudan's Defence Industrial Complex

The Defence Industries System, described by US authorities as Sudan's largest military-industrial enterprise, manages the country's weapons supply chain through complex subsidiary structures including Giad Industrial Group. Both DIS and Giad had already been sanctioned in 2023, but the latest action targets the international networks that continue to funnel materiel into the country despite those earlier restrictions.

The civil war between the SAF and the RSF erupted in April 2023 and has displaced millions, created widespread famine, and drawn accusations of genocide against the RSF from the US government. International ceasefire efforts have repeatedly stalled, with both sides accused of obstructing humanitarian access.

Implications for Indian Business

The sanctioning of an Indian national and company represents a rare direct intersection between India's manufacturing sector and the enforcement of US sanctions policy on African conflicts. SBL Energy operates in Chhattisgarh's industrial sector and appears to have maintained commercial relationships with Sudanese military procurement entities.

The State Department urged foreign governments and private actors to cease all financial and military support to both sides in Sudan's conflict, calling for an immediate unconditional three-month humanitarian truce.

For the Indian diaspora, the case highlights the reach of US sanctions enforcement and the potential risks faced by Indian businesses operating in conflict-adjacent supply chains. India has not publicly commented on the sanctions against Choudhari and SBL Energy.
